acceptance_criteria: The chosen shape is stated, and if no ruling was given the response is BLOCKED with the three options restated.
Every tier in the roster is sourced from the 072-084 traces with its run id quoted, or marked UNPINNED.
The roster is dated and its runs named, with the decay caveat stated.
No price appears anywhere in the artifact.
If Option A: non-negotiable 6 is amended explicitly, the guard still fails on a model id in code, profiles and workflows, and each is demonstrated.
If Option B: no model id appears in .env.example.
The decision is recorded in the notebook as a departure or clarification.
.env was not edited and nothing was paid for — asserted.
Suite passes; count reported before and after.
assumptions: The owner's tier selections are recoverable from the committed 072-084 traces and any pin records. If any tier is not recoverable, it is marked UNPINNED rather than inferred.
constraints: STOP FOR THE OWNER'S RULING on the shape, and do not choose it yourself. Three options are on the table: (A) amend non-negotiable 6 to permit a dated first-run example; (B) ship a placeholder .env.example and record the roster in a dated document beside it; (C) ship real names with the rule unchanged. (C) fails tests/test_docs.py and is advised against. State which you were instructed to implement; if you were not, return BLOCKED with the three options restated.

DO NOT INVENT THE ROSTER. Take the owner's actual selections from the 072-084 traces and any committed pin records — every tier named must be the serving that actually answered it, quoted from the trace with its run id. A roster assembled from a summary rather than from the traces is a hand-stamp.

EVERY TIER MUST BE SOURCED OR MARKED UNKNOWN. Six required tiers exist; the 072-084 runs may not have exercised all six. For any tier with no live evidence, write UNPINNED — and do not fill it from a plausible guess.

THE ROSTER IS DATED AND DECAYS. State the date it was assembled and the runs it is drawn from. State plainly that a roster is a snapshot: ARCH-20260923-071's serving consumed its whole token budget and emitted nothing, and nothing guarantees today's good roster is good next month.
DO NOT WRITE A COST OR PRICE. Non-negotiable 6 bars prices; rates come from the provider catalogue. If a figure is needed, point at the catalogue.

IF OPTION A: amend non-negotiable 6 explicitly, recording what it permitted before and what it permits now, and extend tests/test_docs.py so it still fails on a model id in code, profiles or workflows — prove the extension by breaking it in each of the three places and leaving README and the example permitted.
IF OPTION B: .env.example carries placeholders only, each naming its tier and its function, with a short comment pointing at the dated roster document. State that no model id appears in the example.
RECORD THE DECISION in the notebook: which shape was chosen, the reason, and that a shipped default is a deliberate departure from, or a clarification of, the no-defaults principle.
Do NOT edit .env. The owner owns it (G-3). Do NOT run anything that spends money.
Keep the diff small. Suite reported before and after.

questions: Which shape does the owner rule — A, B or C? This is a ruling because it changes what ships, and I will not choose it for you.

Were all six required tiers exercised in 072-084, or only planning and building? Any tier the runs did not reach must be marked UNPINNED, and that number is itself worth knowing before a new operator configures it.

Should the roster be regenerated from the ledger on a schedule rather than written once? A generated roster cannot go stale silently, which is what convention 24 asks for — state whether the ledger can produce it.
